file_name: Lehmann et al. - 2022 - Designing AINA Intercultural Human Centered Design of an AI based Application for Supporting the Dia.txt

barriers.description: The team could not conduct on-site observations because of the COVID-19 pandemic, preventing direct contextual inquiry in the field.
barriers.justification: This resource constraint directly hindered the designers' ability to understand the context of use and to manage evolving user understanding through in-person observation and field studies.
barriers.reference_excerpt: we wished to conduct additional on-site observations during the analysis and evaluation phases. Unfortunately, this was not possible due to the global COVID-19 pandemic.

barriers.description: Participant availability was severely limited during the study period, with only a few participants available for the full three-month survey.
barriers.justification: Limited participant availability reduced the designers' capacity to facilitate sustained user involvement and to gather longitudinal or iterative feedback needed for synthesis and iteration.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, only a few participants were available for the entire three-month survey period.

barriers.description: Intercontinental and intercultural communication, plus language differences, complicated engagement with on-site user groups and required interpreters.
barriers.justification: These knowledge and language gaps impeded managing deep user understanding and facilitating participatory evaluations because translators and remote communication reduced direct access to users' native-language expressions and nuance.
barriers.reference_excerpt: The particular challenge in this project is the intercontinental and intercultural communication with the user groups on-site since the development team consists of German physicians and computer scientists. Interviews were conducted in English, French, and Malagasy. Interpreters translated from French to English or Malagasy to English when necessary.

barriers.description: Socio-cultural hierarchies and norms caused some participant groups to withhold honest expression in certain settings, undermining participatory methods.
barriers.justification: Power dynamics and cultural norms limited authentic user feedback and participation, hindering the designers' ability to facilitate user involvement and to capture accurate mental models for design decisions.
barriers.reference_excerpt: we first had to learn, with the help of resident physicians, that certain interview settings did not produce the needed outcome because, due to socio-cultural differences, certain groups of people did not express themselves freely or at all in some settings, which is a major problem for participatory design methods. Due to the cross-cultural characteristics of the region, a deliberate attempt for specific user groups was made to reduce the number of participants and homogenize by gender; otherwise, some of the evaluation participants may not express themselves honestly or at all.

barriers.description: Stable IT infrastructure was only partially present in primary health care facilities in the target region.
barriers.justification: Limited local infrastructure constrained designers' ability to study real-world context of use and to run or evaluate remotely shared prototypes reliably, affecting contextual understanding and practical evaluation.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Stable IT infrastructure was only partially present in primary health care facilities.

barriers.description: Regulatory/AI guideline-driven revisions forced technical language to remain in the manual, preventing simplification of documentation.
barriers.justification: This external constraint limited designers' ability to adapt language for target users, hindering management of user understanding and reducing effectiveness of participatory evaluation feedback related to documentation.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Unfortunately, the revision of the manual, based on AI guidelines for medical devices, did not reduce the number of technical terms used, so all users commented negatively on this.
